source.title: Banishing LLM Hallucinations Requires Rethinking Generalization
source.authors: John Li; Saksham Consul; Eda Zhou; J. Wong; N. Farooqui; Yuxin Ye; Nithyashree Manohar; Zhuxiaona Wei; Tian Wu; Benjamin Echols; Sharon Zhou; G. Diamos

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether pretrained language models can fit random answers while retaining performance on unrelated questions, using language-model fine-tuning and QA evaluation rather than the original image-classification setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports random-answer training losses and qualitative held-out QA behavior. Its citations to prior random-label studies are not rows. The MoME training-loss result does not report a corresponding held-out generalization result.
record.test_reason: The study tests part of V1 in a new setting: pretrained language models fit randomized answers while reportedly retaining correct answers to unrelated held-out questions. It does not establish V1's complete natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: pretrained LLMs can fit randomized answers without substantially worsening what they call generalization error, and generalization error does not distinguish hallucination performance. Their evidence for retained held-out performance is qualitative; no numerical train–test error gap is reported.
record.recipe_differences: Language-model fine-tuning on QA data with random character-string answers; Appendix A specifies Llama 3 8B, LoRA, Adafactor and 100 epochs. The study also proposes and tests a MoME architecture.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper discusses results across Llama 3 and Mistral v2 and TruthfulQA and MMLU, but does not report separate numerical outcomes for each combination.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 8 reports approximately equal MMLU scores for models with 0% versus 100% accuracy on a precise-recall task.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Broad benchmark performance can remain similar despite large differences in precise factual recall.

record.code_released: not stated; the text gives a Hugging Face model-weights reference: engineering-lamini/lamini-1-random
record.problems: Held-out performance is described only as mostly unchanged, without numerical accuracy or error estimates. The text does not establish that the evaluation examples are same-distribution natural-label test examples. The MoME result reports training loss but no held-out evaluation.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 gives selected answer examples rather than aggregate performance measurements, so these examples are not separate rows. Figure 2 and other cited works do not report this study's version-specific experimental outcomes.

untested.parts: Held-out accuracy relative to chance under both natural and randomized labels; whether retained answers reflect newly learned generalization rather than pretrained knowledge; the original image-classification architectures and training recipes. MoME held-out generalization is not reported.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizer generalization under matched tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The absence of chance baselines or aggregate held-out scores is an untested component, not evidence of a scope limitation. R3 alone warrants no coexistence verdict.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out accuracy or error against chance is reported; the held-out questions are described as unrelated, not established as same-distribution natural-label examples. The paper does not report the full specified set of architectures or the Inception V3/ImageNet setting.

rows.subject: Llama 3
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned on question-answer data with answers replaced by random 32-bit character strings; appendix specifies 100 epochs, LoRA adaptors and Adafactor.

conditions.value: TruthfulQA; experiments also described as using MMLU

rows.note: Figure caption reports the result; no exact loss value is stated.
rows.check: Measures the random-answer fitting component only. Figure 1 compares true-answer and random-answer tuning of Llama 3, not two architectures. Section 2 describes random 32-character answers, whereas Appendix A inconsistently calls them 32-bit strings. The backbone is frozen and only LoRA adapters are trained.

source_check.correct: True-answer fine-tuning also reaches near-zero training loss after 100 epochs; Figure 1 explicitly reports this for both tuning conditions.
source_check.problem: The baseline is reported qualitatively in the caption, so 'not stated' omits an available comparison.

rows.subject: Llama 3 and Mistral v2
rows.size_stated: Llama 3 8B is stated in Appendix A; Mistral v2 size not stated
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated models fine-tuned on random answers on held-out questions; the text reports the outcome collectively.

conditions.value: held-out standard questions; TruthfulQA and MMLU are named

rows.measure: Answer performance on unrelated held-out questions
rows.note: The paper names both architectures and datasets, but does not give separate model- or dataset-level performance numbers here.
rows.check: The reported retention of held-out answers is qualitative, not an accuracy estimate. 'Mostly unchanged' does not establish an incomplete coexistence effect and therefore does not justify partial. The text names both architectures and datasets but provides no separate outcomes for each combination. Appendix A permits either another subset of the same dataset or another dataset; same-distribution evaluation is not established.

source_check.locator_found: Sections 2–3; Table 1 and its caption; Appendix A

rows.subject: Lamini-1 MoME
rows.size_stated: millions of memory experts; expert-array example uses one million
rows.operation_detail: Repeated the randomization test by memory-tuning on real answers and random answers.
rows.note: This reports training fit only; the paper does not report held-out generalization for this MoME comparison.
rows.check: Measures random-answer fitting only; no corresponding held-out result establishes coexistence for MoME. The architecture uses a frozen pretrained transformer backbone with selected memory experts trained.

relationships.condition: Pretrained LLMs fine-tuned on randomized QA answers, with qualitative evaluation on unrelated held-out questions
relationships.reason: R1 reports near-zero random-answer training loss and R2 reports largely retained held-out answers, supporting coexistence in this setting without establishing the chance-referenced comparison.
relationships.display_finding: The model largely continued to give its previous answers on unrelated held-out examples as training loss on random answers approached zero. This provided qualitative evidence, without a comparison to chance or newly learned natural-label generalization.

tranche.reason: The study extends random-label fitting and retained held-out behavior to pretrained language-model QA, a new setting for part of V1.

source_check.notes: Section 2 describes 32-character answers, whereas Appendix A describes 32-bit strings; the source is internally inconsistent. The authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased, but retained answers provide qualitative evidence rather than a numerical train–test gap or complete V1 comparison.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Llama 3 and Mistral v2 on the reported held-out QA evaluations
reader_labels.reason: Random-answer fine-tuning reportedly leaves unrelated-question performance mostly unchanged (R1–R2), qualitatively supporting coexistence of random-answer fitting and retained QA performance.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The result is qualitative and does not establish test error far below chance on same-distribution natural labels (R2).
